newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: BOXING-WBA STRIPS TYSON OF RANKING PENDING NEVADA DECISION.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-WBA STRIPS TYSON OF RANKING PENDING NEVADA DECISION.

text.p: The World Boxing Association (WBA) has stripped heavyweight Mike Tyson of his ranking following the notorious ear-biting incident with Evander Holyfield, a WBA official said Tuesday.

The decision to remove Tyson from the July 28 rankings followed the Nevada State Boxing Commission's decision to suspend the former world title holder and withhold his $30 million purse pending a final ruling on the case, WBA committee member Israel Sarmiento told Reuters.
"Our guidelines indicate that while a boxer is suspended he is removed from the list of title challengers," Sarmiento said.

Tyson, who until the ill-fated title fight occupied the number one challenger spot behind champion Holyfield, could be re-assigned a ranking after completing any suspension handed down by Nevada commission, which is expected to render a final ruling on Wednesday.

"Tyson is Tyson and his ranking will be reconsidered," Sarmiento said. "The classification committee will study his particular case and he could be included in the rankings again, although not necessarily as number one."
Tyson's spot as top challenger has been taken by South Africa's Frans Botha in the latest WBA rankings.
The WBA has its headquarters in Venezuela where its President Gilberto Mendoza is based.
